messages:
alex: Heads-up — I found an embedding telemetry risk during a routine job. Some customers' short prompts + vectors make it trivial to recover seed text from stored vectors if we keep raw embeddings in logs. We need a concrete sampling + scrub policy and a Console UX for temporary inspect grants.

mia: Can you paste the quick repro and what data we currently store?

alex: Repro: small contrived prompt -> embedding. Our pipeline currently persists `vector` field in request logs before redaction. Example of the proposed policy concept: ```json
{
  "route": "/v1/embeddings",
  "scrub": "hash-truncate",
  "hash_salt": "route-specific",
  "sample_rate": 0.01,
  "inspect_ttl_seconds": 900,
  "retention": "30d"
}
```
This would mean: sample a small fraction pre-routing, scrub stored vectors with a route-specific salt + truncation, and allow a temporary inspect window controlled by Console.

rachel: Hashing+truncation helps but doesn't remove the risk entirely (nearest-neighbor attacks still possible). Strong preference: do not log raw float vectors. If we must, add DP noise or quantize+bucketize before logging. Also require KMS encryption for any stored hashes and mandatory audit trail for inspect grants.

sam: UX notes: Console should expose a per-route toggle: `Allow Embed Inspect` (disabled by default). Oncall flow: request a 15m inspect grant with a required justification field and an approver path (privacy or legal). The Console could show a small CTA: "Request Inspect (15m)" and create an audit-event with approver ping.

mia: Operationally we should sample before routing decision. If we sample after routing into Dedicated pools we risk skewing capacity metrics and misattributing cost. Also embedding logs are large — they blow quotas and telemetry costs fast. So sampling must be upstream.

devops-bot: Deploy Canary: `embed-scrub-policy` -> 5% prod-us-west (rollout id r-1234).

alex: Proposed metric names to add so dashboards can track impacts: `embed_logged_count`, `embed_scrubbed_count`, `embed_inspect_grants`, `embed_inspect_denied`. Add quota guardrail: if `embed_logged_count` > quota threshold, raise an alert and auto-disable inspect grants for that route.

rachel: Add requirement: any inspect grant must be recorded with requestor, approver, justification, and duration. Store audit events in an immutable store and surface them in Console. Also add a retention policy for audit events (90d) and make them exportable to GCP/tenant SIEM via KMS-protected export.

sam: Small Console copy idea: when a user hovers the inspect toggle show: "Inspect grants are temporary, audited, and require approval. Default: OFF. Use only for debugging high-severity incidents." Make the request modal prefill the last 3 incident IDs.

alex: Quick ops command for testing privacy smoke: `./scripts/privacy-smoke --route embeddings --count 1000` — runs synthetic prompts and validates no raw vectors persisted. Please run in staging before canary.

mia: :thumbsup: I'll run the smoke job, then we can flip canary. Also add synthetic PII tests (names, emails) to stress the scrub.

devops-bot: Canary r-1234 started: 5% prod-us-west. Next checkpoint in 2h. Logs: https://internal.ops/r-1234

alex: TL;DR plan I'll put into a short RFC: 1) sample pre-routing (0.5–1%), 2) default scrub/quantize for embeddings + route salt, 3) Console: per-route `Allow Embed Inspect` (temp 15m), request workflow + audit, 4) metrics + quota guardrails + KMS for stored artifacts. Opening RFC now.

rachel: One more ask — include a privacy stress test in the pre-rollout checklist and a small risk matrix in the RFC.

sam: I'll prototype the Console modal (mockups) and the audit event UI.

mia: After smoke + privacy tests pass, we can expand canary to 25% and monitor `embed_scrubbed_count` vs cost.

alex: Thanks all — tagging @product for visibility. Will ping here when RFC link is up.
